headline: Multi-omics reanalyses test reproducibility of disease and aging molecular signatures
label: Multiomics Integration Across Diseases
summary: Reanalysis of public single-cell, bulk and GWAS resources now tests whether disease and aging signatures replicate across studies.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is integrative analysis of public omics resources to test whether molecular signatures generalise. A cross-study reanalysis of four cortical ALS snRNA-seq datasets (140 donors) finds conventional case-control signatures poorly reproducible, while pathology-defined cell states yield reproducible transcriptomic signatures. An adipocyte single-nucleus multiome across 118 donors maps context-dependent cis-regulatory and cellular program QTLs under disease-relevant stimuli. Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis studies harmonise scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, methylation and proteomic layers to nominate cross-layer candidates, while a DKD–PD comparison reports only partial IRF8/TLR7 myeloid convergence. A modular architecture of cellular aging and a GWAS Catalog proxy-trait analysis of sarcopenia extend this to organ-level and trait-level questions. The new element is the emphasis on replication and context: several items report limited overlap rather than convergence.
